programme: Wong/Alexander · conditional owner and ancestry transfer
title: A supplied owner map can preserve ancestry properties under explicit conditions

plain_language.question: When can a supplied map from a rich history to organism owners preserve precise ancestry properties?
plain_language.what_we_learned: Exact ancestry correspondence and finite owner fibres transfer the stated properties under their separate hypotheses. The identical-ancestors property even tolerates finitely many wrong ancestry answers per representative. A merely sound owner map is not enough.
plain_language.what_it_lets_someone_do: Check the exact assumptions needed before transferring a graph-level ancestry conclusion, and distinguish a valid conditional theorem from a claim that owners can be inferred from genomic data.
plain_language.what_cannot_conclude: This does not infer ownership, validate a biological model or classify species empirically. The finite-error relaxation transfers only the identical-ancestors property; maximality equivalence is restricted to whole-owner, saturated candidates.

exact_statement_and_scope: The identical-ancestors property (IAP) means that each member has finitely many descendants or finitely many nondescendants inside the candidate. It is a mathematical graph predicate, not an empirical species label. Let R and E be supplied directed graphs on Nat, let q:Nat→Nat be a supplied owner map, let S be an organism candidate, and let C=q⁻¹(S) contain all rich representatives of those owners. Ancestry means nonempty directed paths. If q is onto, every owner fibre is finite, and ancestry is equivalent for every pair of representatives with different owners, then IAP and reflection agree between C in R and S in E. No uniform fibre bound is required. Reflection means that each candidate member with infinitely many ambient descendants also has infinitely many descendants within the candidate. The exact ancestry hypothesis is both directions for every such representative pair, not mere soundness, exact image edges or an existential lift. Under path soundness alone, an R ancestry path maps to owner equality or E ancestry, and convexity pulls back. With an onto owner map, soundness also transfers a common ancestor downward; weak connectivity descends when S is convex. With onto ownership, exact different-owner ancestry and acyclic E, convexity is equivalent. Adding finite fibres gives descent of the source-defined specieslike predicate, namely nonempty induced-undirected connectivity plus IAP plus ancestral convexity. Adding internal weak connectivity of every owner fibre gives specieslike equivalence on saturated candidates C. Under those stronger premises, target maximality is equivalent to rich maximality among all saturated inverse-image candidates. Unrestricted rich maximality of a saturated C also descends. The reverse implication to unrestricted rich maximality is not asserted. Neither the full biosphere/date/child-count conditions nor the fixed founder-window property is automatically transported. The later finite-error extension proves IAP(R,C) iff IAP(E,S) assuming only onto q, finite fibres and, for each a∈C, finitely many b∈C whose R-ancestry answer differs from E-ancestry(q(a),q(b)). The finite error set and its size may vary with a; no common bound is needed. Errors between different owners are permitted and no agreement outside C is required. This IAP theorem needs neither acyclicity, soundness nor connected fibres. It does not transfer reflection, convexity, connectivity, maximality or specieslike status under those relaxed premises. “Finite errors” refers to transitive ancestry answers, not finitely many edited immediate-parent edges. A proved countercontrol fixes one infinite connected rich fork history and identity ownership. Both the fork pedigree and a chain pedigree are sound interpretations, with onto singleton fibres and the stated natural/real-date biosphere properties; the chain is whole-population specieslike and the fork fails IAP. It shows why soundness cannot replace ancestry equivalence. It is an abstract ancestry countermodel, not identical DNA distributions under a specified diploid inheritance law. The same source also composes the previously indexed finite-gARG opposite-completion theorem with elementary observation-fibre recovery to show that arbitrary deterministic coarsening cannot remove that existing ambiguity. This is credited reuse of CB-GENOME-001, not another newly counted obstruction. The graphs, owners and candidate are mathematical inputs. A finite sampled ARG cannot be onto an infinite organism history. An R path after coordinate erasure can switch loci and need not represent one DNA segment. No owner inference, biological validity, observation likelihood, effective decision procedure or empirical species assignment follows.
